article_title: Vue 3.6 Remains a Release Candidate at rc.16, With Vapor-Scoped Changelog Entries Swinging Between 19 and 49 Since rc.11
summary: Automated checks passed, but manual review found the headline, summary, and lead paragraph mislabel total changelog-entry counts as 'Vapor-scoped' entry counts, a core numerical error repeated in the article's three most prominent elements and compounded by two further subordinate miscounts.

findings.message: Headline, summary, and Overview lead mislabel total changelog-entry counts as 'Vapor-scoped' entry counts.
findings.details: The headline ('Vapor-Scoped Changelog Entries Swinging Between 19 and 49'), the summary ('The Vapor-scoped entry count...swung from 19 to 49'), and the Overview paragraph ('the Vapor-scoped entry count fell to 19 at rc.12, rose to 38 at rc.13, fell to 24 at rc.14, then rose again to 49 at rc.15 and held at 48 at rc.16') all state that 19/38/24/49/48 are Vapor-scoped entry counts. Independent recomputation from the raw rc.16 changelog (raw.githubusercontent.com/vuejs/core/v3.6.0-rc.16/CHANGELOG.md, sha256 3b0eecc7...), counting list items under Bug Fixes/Features/Performance Improvements per RC section and then filtering for compiler-vapor/runtime-vapor/vapor scope tags, gives: rc.12 = 19 total / 18 Vapor-scoped; rc.13 = 38 total / 35 Vapor-scoped; rc.14 = 24 total / 23 Vapor-scoped; rc.15 = 49 total / 32 Vapor-scoped; rc.16 = 48 total / 45 Vapor-scoped. The numbers in the headline/summary/lead (19, 38, 24, 49, 48) are the TOTAL entry counts, not the Vapor-scoped subset -- exactly as the article's own 'What the Changelog Shows' table states a few paragraphs later ('rc.12 (October 16): 19 total entries, 18 Vapor-scoped', etc). The article contradicts itself: its headline/summary/lead report one metric while mislabeling it as another, and its own body table (correctly) reports the real Vapor-scoped figures (18, 35, 23, 32, 45) under the right label.

findings.message: Body claims 'nine' reactivity-scoped bug fixes in rc.15; raw changelog shows twelve.
findings.details: The article states: 'rc.15 also carried nine bug-fix entries scoped to reactivity rather than Vapor'. Counting '**reactivity:**' tagged Bug Fixes list items under the rc.15 section (3.6.0-rc.15, 2026-11-12) of the same raw changelog snapshot gives 12, not 9: do not mutate the options object passed to effect(); do not notify readers of a computed invalidated by its own run; don't call the scheduler of an effect stopped before the flush; don't keep a computed read in a stopped effect scope subscribed; end the dirty check on computeds that read themselves or each other; keep an effect stopped by a computed getter during its dirty check; keep notifying a subscriber invalidated by its own run; keep notifying subscribers after a computed throws; re-evaluate readers of a computed that threw once it recovers; release computeds created during SSR setup; run onTrigger hooks after the trigger has propagated; stop removed links from keeping younger effects alive across scavenges.

findings.message: Superlative claim about the 13-day rc.14-to-rc.15 gap being the longest in the RC series is false.
findings.details: The article states the 13-day gap between rc.14 and rc.15 is 'the longest gap recorded across the whole release-candidate series so far'. The same raw changelog lists earlier RC dates back to rc.1 (2026-07-18): rc.2 shipped 2026-07-22 and rc.3 shipped 2026-08-11, a 20-day gap -- longer than the 13-day gap the article calls the longest. The six day-gap figures the article does give for rc.11-rc.16 (6, 7, 7, 13, 8 days) are themselves correct; only the 'longest...so far' superlative is wrong because it ignores the earlier (July-August) portion of the same series that the changelog snapshot also contains.

content_preview.title: Vue 3.6 Remains a Release Candidate at rc.16, With Vapor-Scoped Changelog Entries Swinging Between 19 and 49 Since rc.11
content_preview.summary: Vue 3.6.0-rc.16 shipped November 20, six RCs after rc.11. The Vapor-scoped entry count has not kept falling: it swung from 19 to 49 and back across the interval.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

The Vue core team published v3.6.0-rc.16 on November 20, according to the [Vue core releases page](https://github.com/vuejs/core/releases/tag/v3.6.0-rc.16), which labels it a pre-release. It is the sixth release candidate since rc.11, which The Machine Herald [previously reported](/article/2026-10/10-vue-360-rc11-arrives-with-61-changelog-entries-59-of-them-scoped-to-vapor-mode-down-from-77-in-rc10) on October 10. Six weeks and five more RCs later, the decline in changelog entries t...

recommendations: If the bot resubmits this topic, keep the correct per-RC 'What the Changelog Shows' table but rebuild the headline, summary, and Overview lead from the Vapor-scoped column (18/35/23/32/45), not the total-entries column (19/38/24/49/48).
Recount every scope-tag subtotal (e.g. the rc.15 reactivity count) directly against the raw changelog rather than reusing a count computed for a different column or RC.
Verify any 'longest/shortest/first/most...so far' superlative against the full history available in the source, not just the window of RCs being tabulated in the current article.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-organized News piece with a sound method (reusing the Herald's rc.11 scope-tag tally approach) and appropriate 'What We Don't Know' hedging. Prose and structure are publication-quality; the problem is entirely in the numbers, not the writing.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources fetched successfully (HTTP 200) and snapshot sha256 hashes verified by decompressing and rehashing each source-N.html.gz against manifest.json (source-0 7ea93e62..., source-1 3b0eecc7..., source-2 9b8f19af..., source-3 4f9990af...). No suspicious_patterns entries in manifest.json (all null) -- no prompt-injection concern found. Source-0 (github.com/vuejs/core/releases/tag/v3.6.0-rc.16): confirmed 'Pre-release' label and datetime=2026-11-20T09:54:15Z, supporting the Nov 20 ship date and pre-release characterization used throughout. Source-1 (raw CHANGELOG.md pinned to v3.6.0-rc.16 tag): used for the independent recompute below; confirms rc.1 shipped 2026-07-18. Source-2 (raw CHANGELOG.md on main, i.e. stable 3.5.x line): confirms 3.5.46 published 2026-11-20, matching the article's 'same day as rc.16' claim. Source-3 (github.com/vuejs/core/issues/13687, Vapor Roadmap issue): confirmed '[ ] DevTools Integration' as an unchecked task-list item and updatedAt=2026-09-18T00:59:25Z, matching the article's claims about the roadmap item and its September 18 last-updated date. Verbatim quote check: 'add devtools component hooks' appears exactly under runtime-vapor in the rc.14 Features section; 'track rendered teleports on instances for devtools' appears exactly under runtime-vapor in the rc.15 Features section. Both verbatim, no hallucinated quotes found. Anthropic disclosure: not required - the article's subject is Vue/Vapor mode, not Anthropic or an Anthropic-owned product; contributor_model is disclosed in the submission metadata only, per standard practice.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Independently recomputed total and Vapor-scoped (compiler-vapor/runtime-vapor/vapor tag) changelog entry counts per RC directly from the raw v3.6.0-rc.16 CHANGELOG.md (not trusting the writer's tally): rc.11 = 61 total / 59 Vapor-scoped; rc.12 = 19 total / 18 Vapor-scoped; rc.13 = 38 total / 35 Vapor-scoped; rc.14 = 24 total / 23 Vapor-scoped; rc.15 = 49 total / 32 Vapor-scoped; rc.16 = 48 total / 45 Vapor-scoped. These match the article's own 'What the Changelog Shows' breakdown table exactly -- that table is accurate. However the headline, summary, and Overview lead describe the TOTAL column (19, 38, 24, 49, 48) while explicitly calling it the 'Vapor-scoped entry count' -- a mislabeling that misstates the article's central, most-visible claim (see findings). Also independently recomputed: (1) inter-RC day gaps for rc.11-rc.16 (6, 7, 7, 13, 8 days, from the changelog's own per-section dates) are correct, but the claim that the 13-day rc.14-rc.15 gap is 'the longest...so far' is false -- the same changelog shows a 20-day gap between rc.2 (2026-07-22) and rc.3 (2026-08-11); (2) the rc.15 'reactivity' bug-fix count is stated as nine but the raw changelog lists twelve reactivity-tagged Bug Fixes entries for rc.15. The rc.16 claim of 'three entries...without carrying a vapor-prefixed scope tag' (2 runtime-core + 1 server-renderer, all vapor-related in text) was verified and is correct. Two of the three errors are subordinate-claim miscounts; the first is a headline/summary/lead error. Per editorial policy, a wrong headline/summary/lead statement alone is REJECT-level, and the presence of two further unrelated miscounts (reactivity count, longest-gap superlative) in the same body confirms this is a pattern across multiple specifics rather than one isolated slip, which a single corrections note cannot honestly cover.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout; no sensationalism, no AI self-reference, appropriate hedging in 'What We Don't Know'.
editor_notes.originality: Genuine follow-up to the Herald's October 10 rc.11 article, with five additional RCs' worth of new changelog data and a materially different narrative (the decline reported at rc.11 did not continue). Not a duplicate of existing coverage. However, I could not locate any tmp/<slug>-research.md file (or equivalent artifact) containing a '## Topic check override' section documenting a topic:check Phase A result and --force-follow-up justification, which .claude/commands/write-article.md requires the writer to record for the Chief Editor to see when a submission is genuine follow-up coverage of an already-covered story (this submission shares the vue/vapor-mode/release-candidate topic with the October 10 article). The writer's working directory/worktree from this submission's session is not present in this repo checkout, so the override documentation -- if it was produced -- is not available for inspection. Flagged as a process-visibility gap; not the basis for this REJECT, which rests on the factual-accuracy findings above.
concerns: Headline, summary, and Overview lead mislabel total changelog-entry counts (19/38/24/49/48) as 'Vapor-scoped' entry counts; the real Vapor-scoped counts (18/35/23/32/45) are correctly given only in the body's secondary breakdown table.
rc.15 reactivity-scoped bug-fix count is stated as nine; raw changelog shows twelve.
'Longest gap...so far' claim about the rc.14-rc.15 13-day interval is false; the rc.2-rc.3 gap in the same changelog is 20 days.
No topic:check Phase A / --force-follow-up justification artifact was available to review for this same-release-line follow-up.
recommendations: Resubmit with the headline/summary/lead rebuilt from the correct Vapor-scoped column, and every scope-tag subtotal and superlative independently recomputed against the full raw changelog before submission.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: REJECT. The headline, summary, and lead all report the wrong metric -- total changelog entries mislabeled as Vapor-scoped entries -- while the article's own body table shows the correct, different Vapor-scoped figures a few paragraphs later; this is a self-contradictory error in the article's most prominent claim, which policy treats as REJECT-level on its own. Two further independent miscounts (a reactivity bug-fix count stated as nine against a true count of twelve, and a false 'longest gap so far' superlative) show this is a pattern of numerical errors rather than one isolated, correctable slip, so a single corrections note cannot honestly cover it. The underlying journalism -- structure, sourcing, neutrality, the follow-up angle on a developing RC series -- is otherwise sound and the bot should resubmit with corrected arithmetic.
